Rashi on Berakhot 40b:10:1.english: From blessing You - [By reciting:] "Blessed [are You, Lord our God, King of the Universe,] Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to separate terumah and tithe."

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:12:1.english: The novelot - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:12:3.english: A type of curse - Vinegar, novelot, and locusts come about through a curse.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:14:1.english: That turned sour - *Botir*, in Old French.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:15:1.english: With regard to growth, they grow from the earth - From the moisture of the earth, they grow on wood and on vessels.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:17:1.hebrew: בושלי כמרא - כמו שרופי חמה, שבשלם ושרפם החום ויבשו, ותמרים הם. כמרא — חום, כמו מכמר בשרא (פסחים דף נח.):
Rashi on Berakhot 40b:17:1.english: Ripened by heat - Like sun-scorched [produce], which the heat ripened and scorched and they dried up, and they are dates. Khamra [means] heat, as in "mikhmar bisra" [the heating of the meat] (Pesachim 58a).

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:17:2.english: Dates of the wind - That the wind causes them to fall.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:19:1.english: On the rest - Rabbi Yehuda disagrees regarding vinegar and locusts.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:20:1.hebrew: פרי העץ בעי ברוכי - שהרי לא נשתנו לקלקול:
Rashi on Berakhot 40b:20:1.english: One should recite [the blessing of] the fruit of the tree - For they did not change for the worse.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:21:1.hebrew: הקלים שבדמאי - פירוש: שהקלו חכמים בדמאי שלהן, שהלוקחן מעם הארץ אין צריך לעשרן. אלו הן:
Rashi on Berakhot 40b:21:1.english: The lenient [items] with regard to demai - [The] explanation [is] that the Sages were lenient with regard to their demai, in that one who purchases them from an am ha'aretz does not need to tithe them. These are they:

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:21:2.hebrew: השיתין כו' - שאינן חשובים, ואין ע"ה חש עליהם מלעשרן:
Rashi on Berakhot 40b:21:2.english: The shittin, etc. - For they are not important, and an am ha'aretz does not begrudge tithing them.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:22:2.english: The end of the vines - Autumn grapes.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:23:1.english: Whereas their definitely untithed [produce] - If it is known that tithes were not separated from them.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:24:1.hebrew: שעשאן גורן - העני או מי שלקטן, העמיד מהן ערימת כרי:
Rashi on Berakhot 40b:24:1.english: That he made them [into] a threshing floor - The poor person, or whoever gathered them, set up from them a heap [like] a grain-pile.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:24:2.hebrew: הלקט והשכחה והפאה - אע"פ שפטורים מן המעשר, לקטן עני ועשאן גורן — הוקבעו למעשר מדרבנן, דמאן דחזי סבר שתבואת קרקעו היא:
Rashi on Berakhot 40b:24:2.english: The gleanings, the forgotten sheaves, and the corner [of the field] - Even though they are exempt from tithes, [if] a poor person gathered them and made them [into] a threshing floor, they are rendered obligated in tithes rabbinically, for whoever sees [it] will think that it is the produce of his [own] land.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:2:1.hebrew: חוץ מן הפת ומן היין - כדאמרינן לקמן (ברכות דף מב.), שגורם ברכות הרבה לעצמו — בקדוש, ובהבדלה, ובברכת חתנים:
Rashi on Berakhot 40b:2:1.english: Except for bread and wine - As we say below (Berakhot 42a), [wine] causes many blessings for itself — at Kiddush, at Havdalah, and at the wedding blessings.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:7:1.english: The obligation of the first blessing - The blessing of HaZan [Who sustains].

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:9:1.english: The portion of the sotah - When the priest adjures her.

Rashi on Berakhot 40b:9:2.english: The confession of the tithe - “I have removed the sacred [portion] from the house” (Deuteronomy 26:13).

Tosafot on Berakhot 40b:10:1.hebrew: אמר אביי כוותיה דרב מסתברא כו' - י"מ, דמסתברא ברייתא כוותיה. ומיהו רב אלפס פסק כר' יוחנן, וכן פסק ר"י, דכל ברכה שאין בה מלכות שמים אינה ברכה. ולכך היה אומר ר"י, שאם היה מדלג מלכות של ברכת המוציא שצריך לחזור ולברך; ואפי' דלג תיבת העולם בלבד, דמלך לבד אינו מלכות. וברכות של שמונה עשרה אין בהן מלכות, דאינן באין בפתיחה, ובחתימה אין שייך מלכות; אבל אלהי אברהם הוי כמו מלכות, דאברהם אבינו המליך הקב"ה על כל העולם, שהודיע מלכותו. ומעין שבע דמצלי בשבת — הואיל ויש בה האל הקדוש שאין כמוהו, היינו כמו מלכות, כמו "שמע ישראל ה' אלהינו ה' אחד", דהוי במקום מלכות; ולפי מה דפרישית, דכל היכא דכתיב אלהי אברהם הוי כמו מלכות — ניחא. ולר' יוחנן לא קשיא דלא תני מלכותך, דאטו כרוכלא כל האי לימני וליזיל:
Tosafot on Berakhot 40b:10:1.english: "Abaye said: It stands to reason in accordance with Rav, etc." - Some explain that [this means] the baraita stands to reason in accordance with him [Rav]. However, Rav Alfas [the Rif] ruled in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan, and so ruled the Ri, that any blessing that does not contain [mention of] the sovereignty of Heaven is not a blessing. And therefore the Ri would say that if one omitted the [mention of] sovereignty in the blessing of HaMotzi, he must go back and recite the blessing [again]; and even if he omitted only the word "ha'olam" [the universe], for "melekh" [King] alone is not [an expression of] sovereignty. And the blessings of the Shemoneh Esreh do not contain [mention of] sovereignty, because they do not have an opening [formula], and in the conclusion [formula] sovereignty is not applicable. However, "God of Abraham" is considered like sovereignty, because Abraham our father crowned the Holy One, blessed be He, over the entire world, by making His sovereignty known. And [as for the blessing of] Me'ein Sheva that is prayed on Shabbat — since it contains "the holy God that there is none like Him," this is considered like sovereignty, just like "Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is One," which takes the place of sovereignty. And according to what I explained — that wherever "God of Abraham" is written it is considered like sovereignty — it is [already well] resolved [for Me'ein Sheva also begins with "God of Abraham"]. And according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, it is not difficult that [the baraita] did not teach "Your sovereignty" — for is [the tanna] like a peddler, that he should go on and enumerate all this?!

Tosafot on Berakhot 40b:2:1.hebrew: ורבי יוחנן אמר אפי' פת ויין - וכן הלכה, דרב ור' יוחנן — הלכה כר' יוחנן, וכ"ש לגבי רב הונא, שהיה תלמידו של רב:
Tosafot on Berakhot 40b:2:1.english: "And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even bread and wine" - And so is the halakhah, for [in a dispute between] Rav and Rabbi Yoḥanan, the halakhah follows Rabbi Yoḥanan; and all the more so regarding Rav Huna, who was a student of Rav.

Tosafot on Berakhot 40b:3:1.hebrew: נימא רב הונא כר' יוסי - וא"ת: היכי מצי סובר רב הונא כר' יוסי? הא רב הונא מודה בשאר דברים, חוץ מפת ויין, שאם אמר שהכל — דיצא, ואילו ר' יוסי סבר דלא יצא, דכל המשנה ממטבע כו'! וי"מ, דמצי למימר דאפי' ר' יוסי לא קאמר לא יצא אלא בברוך המקום, שאינה ברכה כלל; אבל בשהכל — מודה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 40b:3:1.english: "Let us say that Rav Huna [holds] in accordance with Rabbi Yosei" - And if you say: How can Rav Huna hold in accordance with Rabbi Yosei? Behold, Rav Huna concedes regarding other items, except for bread and wine, that if one said "Shehakol," he fulfilled [his obligation]; whereas Rabbi Yosei holds that he did not fulfill [his obligation], for "Anyone who alters the formula [coined by the Sages in blessings does not fulfill his obligation]"! And some explain that [the Gemara] could say that even Rabbi Yosei only said "he did not fulfill [his obligation]" regarding "Blessed is the Omnipresent," which is not a blessing at all; but regarding "Shehakol," he concedes [that one fulfills his obligation].
